step: ROADMAP S2 (Stage B: the phone's mask-window occupants read off native pixels, for the encounter comparison at a read seed)
claimLevel: DEVICE_MEASURED retained native frames; labels by an agent's visual inspection of 2.5x brightened right-eyehole crops
question: Where is the mask view's right eyehole in native pixels, can a native rule tell the mask view and an occupied eyehole from the rest, and are the retained frames enough to calibrate the occupant classes?
exploratory: A placement and separation study; no detector threshold is claimed for production.

frames.source: every retained FNaF 2 campaign lifecycle frame (artifacts/campaign-2026-*/*lifecycle-observe.py.png, gitignored; 2,208 at 2400x1080), named here by sha256 only
frames.method: per frame: the grid reader eyehole_letter on point samples taken as the Companion takes them ((2c+1)W/40, (2r+1)H/18), the right eyehole interior sampled at step 4 (lit = Rec. 601 luma over 20), the top band y 40-300 at step 4 and 8, the bottom bars at y 1004-1044; mask-view frames then cropped (x 1200-1920, y 360-680), brightened 2.5x and labelled by eye on contact sheets

placement.gridEquivalent: the grid reader's rows 3-5, columns 11-18 sample x 1380-2220, y 420-660: partly the dark mask beyond the eyehole (it ends near x 1900)

gate.rule: mask view = mean luma of y 40-300 under 3 (the mask hides ceiling and posters), no bright bottom-right camera bar (under 1% of x 1220-2330, y 1004-1044 above 150), the bottom-left mask bar present

separation.eyeLit: fraction of the interior (step 4) with luma over 20

reading.gate: The mask view is told from the office and the cameras by its dark top band and missing camera bar; the bottom-left bar strip alone is not enough (office frames share it).
reading.occupancy: Empty and occupied eyeholes separate on lit fraction with a wide gap on these frames.
reading.classes: Only 10 occupied frames (7 yellow, 2 blue, 1 orange-brown): the lifecycle observer samples a frame every few seconds and rarely during an occupied mask window. Too few to calibrate occupant classes; the grid reader's hue rule also cannot tell Toy Chica from Withered Chica, which the model codes c and C.
reading.next: A Stage B night records the right eyehole interior as a REGION beside the static view (one recorder, one combined set: the Companion's regions are one shared set and a second client's clear() would wipe the static recorder's), so occupant classes calibrate on every frame of each mask window.
